QuestionStmt.S: In the diagram shown, the resistance between points A and B is '$R_1$' when an ideal diode D is forward biased and is '$R_2$' when ideal diode D is reverse biased. The ratio $R_1 / R_2$ is

Solution.S:
When the ideal diode D is forward biased, it behaves like a wire. So its resistance is 0 Ω.

In this case, the upper branch becomes a 30 Ω resistor directly connected between A and B. The lower branch also has a 30 Ω resistor between A and B.

So, the two 30 Ω resistors are in parallel.

The equivalent resistance is:

$$R_1 = \frac{30 \times 30}{30 + 30} = 15 \, \Omega$$

When the ideal diode D is reverse biased, it behaves like an open switch. So current cannot pass through the upper branch.

Only the lower 30 Ω resistor remains connected between A and B.

So,

$$R_2 = 30 \, \Omega$$

Now the required ratio is:

$$\frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{15}{30} = \frac{1}{2}$$
